The plan is not only about advertising. The strongest adoption path is social: teacher creates class, students join together, competition makes it enjoyable, and repeated value supports subscription.

This slide helps the team avoid saying only 'our users are students.'
Students are the primary learning users; teachers are early adopters and distribution partners; parents and institutions are trust and payment routes.
Tie every feature back to one persona. Learning journey helps students. Reports help teachers. Family plan helps parents.

KWD's differentiation is not only one feature. It is Khmer-first content, structured learning, gamified practice, teacher tools, AI help, and web access without installation.
The moat answer should be: content depth, teacher/student network, saved progress, and local trust.

For non-technical teammates, simplify this slide: KWD is web-based, works on phones, uses a database, has AI help, supports live play, and protects user data.
For technical questions, mention Next.js, Neon PostgreSQL, Drizzle, Pusher, KHQR, JWT, TOTP 2FA, HTTPS/TLS, and PDPA.
Connect tech to adoption: speed, low data, mobile access, classroom join, and trust.

text:
Explain the pricing as a ladder, not a wall.
Free helps students start. Paid plans are for adults and institutions who need tracking, management, scale, or certification.
If asked how pricing was decided, say the tiers match buyer type and unlock needs: family tracking, teacher reporting, school scale, driving school certificates.

text:
State clearly that these are forward projections from the plan, not completed results.
The paid subscriber path is 100 in 2026, 250 in 2027, and 500 in 2028.
The ARR path is 12,360 dollars, 31,000 dollars, and 62,000 dollars. The source says costs stay low at roughly 80, 300, and 900 dollars, supporting early break-even.

text:
The source document includes judge questions in ten categories: problem, solution/technology, users/testing, adoption, ethics, learning/teamwork, future, business/finance, growth/scaling, and competition.
Practice answer formula: direct answer, proof point, next step. Example: Our target user is students 12 to 18, but teachers are our early adoption channel because they create classes and invite groups. Our next step is to run more school demos and measure retention.
Remind the team to keep answers short, clear, and easy to translate.
